summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of the Work page, AI Mode RAG search, and home navigation. All 10 backend pytest cases pass (root/stats, grounded LLM answers for VantaAI & graph theory, 5 easter eggs, no-hallucination guard). All frontend flows verified: /work renders with 5 project cards & filters work; /ai-mode shows indexed stats, starter questions, easter-egg chips produce 'hidden archive matched' label, custom unknown queries return the no-hallucination 'I could not find enough verified information' text with closest archive + sources. Home hero buttons and tabs route to /work and /ai-mode correctly. No console errors observed.

minor.issue: Backend logs show several 'Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 0.009366, Max budget: 0.001' errors from litellm during the test run. The code falls back to stitching the top archive snippet (still grounded=True) — tests still pass because the snippet contains relevant keywords. After fallbacks, subsequent LLM calls completed successfully, but the EMERGENT_LLM_KEY appears to have intermittent budget exhaustion. Worth monitoring; if budget is hard-capped, LLM answers will degrade silently to stitched snippets without surfacing any error to the user.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Verify Emergent LLM key budget is not capped at $0.001 (logs show 'Max budget: 0.001' budget_exceeded errors triggering fallback path during testing). If this happens in production the LLM response degrades silently to a stitched archive snippet. Consider surfacing a subtle 'fallback mode' label when grounded is True but LLM was unavailable, OR confirm with Emergent that the production key has higher limits.
critical_code_review_comments: knowledge_base.py uses TF-IDF with cosine similarity — correctly returns [] (no contexts) for unrelated queries like 'pizza toppings', which triggers the proper 'could not find enough verified information' fallback in _llm_answer. Hallucination guard is sound.

_llm_answer fallback when LLM throws returns grounded=True with stitched archive text — this silently masks LLM outages from clients. Minor: consider returning grounded=False or adding a 'fallback' flag so the UI could show a subtle indicator.

ai_search endpoint runs synchronous TF-IDF in async path — acceptable for current 20-chunk corpus but will become blocking if corpus grows. Consider running in a thread pool above a few hundred chunks.
server.py easter_egg matching uses substring 'in' check on lowercased query. The phrase '2am' would match queries like 'is it 2am yet' — works as designed but worth noting for SEO-style queries.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all 7 flows pass: /work render, filter, card->detail nav, /ai-mode stats, starter LLM answer, easter egg label, no-hallucination unknown query, tabs, home hero buttons)

seed_data_creation: None — knowledge base is read-only JSON

Re-run with: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_ai_search.py -v. LLM is currently working but backend logs intermittently show 'Budget has been exceeded' from litellm — the _llm_answer fallback path masks this. Frontend selectors verified: data-testid='work-page', work-result-{vanta-ai|del-ai|faimer|lawgorithm|studybee}, work-filter-{all|AI|NLP|...}, ai-mode-page, ai-search-input, ai-search-submit, ai-answer-card, ai-sources, ai-source-N, ai-closest-archive, egg-midnight-thoughts (and other eggs), hero-projects-btn, see-all-projects.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no bugs found. The only environmental observation is the Emergent LLM key occasionally hitting a $0.001 budget cap mid-test, which the code handles gracefully via archive-snippet fallback.
